claim: Humans rarely retrieve a useful earlier case on their own. Retrieval is driven by surface similarity. In Gick and Holyoak only about 41% applied the convergence solution without a hint, about 85% with a hint to use the earlier problem; in Gentner et al. surface-matched probes cued recall 55% vs 12% for relational matches; in Loewenstein 10 of 16 were reminded of a prior case but only 3 of 16 used its principle. GAP SEARCH UPDATE: not universal. Raynal et al. 2026 (N=133 and N=81) replicate surface dominance when both match types exist (close 0.47 vs distant 0.09 per participant) but find pure structure matches beat pure surface matches (0.46 vs 0.04) when the cue is a familiar relational category. A 2026 Fortress-to-Radiation conceptual re-run (N=128) found 5% spontaneous and 36% hinted success with one story, not the 41% and 85% quoted above (those two originals are still second-hand).
agent_test: Library retrieval by surface-only similarity should miss relational matches. Compare surface embedding vs relation-described keys at equal tokens on a subgoal library.

claim: Explicitly comparing two worked cases (versus reading them in turn) raises transfer of the shared principle: contingency contract used by 13/27 compare dyads (48%) vs 5/31 (16%); intensive training lifted a trained principle to 38% (tradeoff) and 69% (contingency) from 6 to 19%. Gain is principle-specific. Adding an abstract label did not help.
agent_test: Before reuse, make the agent write what two stored cases share, store that, and retrieve by it; compare with raw retrieval at equal tokens.

claim: In LLM agents, retrieving similar past successful trajectories as in-context examples beats no memory and beats random examples, usually. ALFWorld (gpt-3.5): ReAct 40.0, random 42.5, task-similarity 59.0. TravelPlanner, KATE and driving studies agree in direction. Random cases can fall below no memory (Memp hard-constraint 6.72 vs 12.88; Gan one random example below zero-shot; Dynamic Cheatsheet retrieval hurt GPT-4o on GPQA and MMLU-Pro).
agent_test: Subgoal library: arm A no library, B random cases, C similarity cases, same tokens. Expect C > A, and watch B < A.

claim: Choice of retrieval key matters. In ExpeL, ranking by task similarity beat reasoning-step similarity (59.0 vs 48.5 on ALFWorld). The paper text calls the reasoning-similarity drop slight, but the table gap is 10.5 points. No second source tests the same contrast; Memp's key=query vs key=AveFact results are mixed. GAP SEARCH UPDATE: two more sources show the key matters. Skill-KNN (LLM-written skill description as key) beat the best raw-text key on Spider 78.3 vs 74.6 and was best non-oracle on 5 datasets; EPR (retriever trained on measured usefulness) beat BM25 by 5 to 8 points (BREAK 31.9 vs 26.0). The three agree that the key should describe what a case is useful for, not how it looks; none tests subgoals.
agent_test: Test keying the subgoal library by problem statement vs by the plan or reasoning trace.

claim: Experience-following: agents copy the output of the most similar retrieved case, so wrong stored cases are repeated and re-stored. Adding every run to memory hurts versus strict addition (RegAgent 55.48 vs 70.95; EHRAgent 13.05 vs 38.50; AgentDriver 32.32 vs 51.00; CIC-IoT 59.90 vs 85.40; fixed memory 67.53, 16.75, 40.11, 71.50). Appending full history also hurt in Dynamic Cheatsheet, some added trajectories lowered performance in Sarukkai, and Evo-Memory saw baselines degrade with unfiltered failures. GAP SEARCH UPDATE: Evo-Memory with failures stored: Gemini 2.5 Flash ALFWorld ExpRAG success 0.59 to 0.25. MINJA wrote wrong cases into memory through ordinary queries (injection success 98.2%, attack success 76.8%); AgentPoison needed under 0.1% poisoned entries for about 80% attack success. No honest 10-to-50-percent dose-response exists.
agent_test: Compare add-all vs add-only-verified to the library, same token budget; log how often a wrong stored plan is copied.

claim: Gating the Retain step by verified outcome or measured downstream utility beats blind accumulation: strict addition and history-based deletion (Xiong), utility-ranked exemplars (Sarukkai, ALFWorld 0.72 fixed, about 0.91 bootstrap, 0.93 curated), verified skills only (Voyager).
agent_test: Admit a subgoal solution only if code verified it on unfitted checks (G3); track retrieval-weighted outcome per case and drop low scorers.

claim: How noisy a success judge can be is contested. Xiong: a coarse LLM judge was worse than a small strict set and gaps widen. ReasoningBank: a judge at 72.7% accuracy and simulated 50 to 100% gave success 47 to 49.7, so robust. The setups differ (task type, memory format); ReasoningBank is a simulation on one subset. GAP SEARCH UPDATE: still contested. No source varies the wrong-case share between 10 and 50 percent; new evidence only adds the all-failures-stored extreme (d13) and adversarial poison (d06, d07).
agent_test: Inject known-wrong cases at 10, 30 and 50% into the library and measure the accuracy loss with code-verified vs model-judged admission.

claim: A small number of retrieved cases is best, and more adds noise. Memento DeepResearcher avg F1/PM: K=0 59.9/72.2, K=1 63.6/77.9, K=4 64.5/78.5 (best), K=32 63.9/78.1; most of the gain comes from the first case. Memp success rises then declines with number retrieved; Sarukkai gains diminish after the first quarter of added tasks; Gan: DeepSeek-R1 14B got worse with more examples. GAP SEARCH UPDATE: best K depends on example quality. Many-shot ICL (Gemini 1.5 Pro, MATH500): human-solution examples peak near 125 then fall; correct-answer-filtered model solutions plateau near 25 at about +5 points and do not fall. Not retrieved by similarity, K counted in examples not tokens.
agent_test: Sweep k=1,2,4,8 at equal total tokens; pick k on a held-out set, not the test set (Memento tuned K on its test data).

claim: Storing abstracted units (workflows, strategies, procedures) rather than raw trajectories is claimed to help, but this is contested. Own-group results: AWM WebArena 35.5 vs 23.5; ReasoningBank 48.8 vs Synapse 42.1 vs AWM 44.1 (flash); Memp proceduralization 77.86 vs trajectory 74.29 vs script 56.43 on ALFWorld. Against: ExpeL ALFWorld retrieval-only 55% beat insights-only 50%; in the independent ReasoningBank run AWM was +3.6, +0.9, -0.9 (not the +12 reported by AWM); AWM gave no gain on the cross-website subset. GAP SEARCH UPDATE: a second non-author run (Evo-Memory, Gemini 2.5 Flash, 4 embodied sets) has AWM at 0.30/0.53 success/progress, same as History, versus ExpRAG raw retrieval 0.46/0.63. Dynamic Cheatsheet's own table: curated memory beats raw retrieval on AIME for Claude (50.0/46.7 vs 43.3) but raw retrieval fell below the memory-free prompt in several GPT-4o cells (AIME 2024 26.7 vs 36.7; MMLU-Pro Eng 48.8 vs 51.6). Verdict stays contested; no independent win for distillation.
agent_test: Same agent, library of (a) raw solved subgoal traces, (b) one-line distilled strategies, (c) both; equal tokens; test on templated and on cross-domain items separately.

claim: Failure cases help only if stored in a format that can use them. ReasoningBank: Synapse 40.6 to 41.7 with failures, AWM degraded, ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7. ExpeL: insights from the few-shot examples alone gave no gain over ReAct while success/failure pairs did. Evo-Memory: unfiltered failures degrade baselines.
agent_test: Store failure as a lesson tied to the failing output (G2), not as raw trace; compare.

claim: Learned or bandit retrieval adds only a small gain over plain similarity. Memento Q-learned retrieval: 85.44 vs 84.85 similarity vs 84.47 no CBR at round 5 (margin shrinks, no variance). CASCADE: 66.68 vs 63.76 average success on Qwen3-32B, about 3 points. Both are the authors' own methods.
agent_test: Only after the plain library works: add an explore/exploit score on cases and test whether it pays for its setup cost (G7).

claim: Memory gain depends on how much tasks share structure. Evo-Memory: gain vs within-dataset task similarity r=0.717 (Gemini 2.5 Flash), 0.563 (Claude 3.7 Sonnet), big on PDDL and ALFWorld, small on AIME-25 and GPQA. ALFWorld has templated tasks; AWM and ReasoningBank gains vanish on cross-website subsets; the Game of 24 jump is reuse of one solution. GAP SEARCH UPDATE: Buffer of Thoughts' largest gains are Game of 24 (GPT-4 3.0 to 82.4, but program-writing PAL already 64.0) and Checkmate-in-One; Evo-Memory shows memory below no-memory success on BabyAI (0.52 to 0.56 vs 0.61).
agent_test: Route to the library only when similarity to the nearest stored case passes a threshold; otherwise skip lookup. Measure gain by similarity bin.

claim: Whether weak models benefit from case reuse is contested. Against: self-recalled analogs fail for weak models (Yasunaga), DS-Agent GPT-3.5 one-shot not better than zero-shot, Gan DeepSeek-R1 14B worsens with examples, ExpeL gpt-3.5 insights worse than gpt-4. For: Evo-Memory says smaller models benefit most.
agent_test: Run the library with a small and a strong model; report the gain per model.

claim: Asking the model to recall its own analogous problems (no store) gives small gains for strong models: GSM8K GPT-3.5 75.8 CoT to 77.8; MATH 34.9 to 37.3; Codeforces GPT-4 about equal to 3-shot (16 vs 16). Small, single paper, 2023 models.
agent_test: Compare self-recall of 3 analogs vs retrieved stored cases at equal tokens on our benchmarks.

claim: Revising a retrieved case from execution feedback matters beyond retrieval. DS-Agent (GPT-4, Kaggle tasks, five repeats): average best rank full 2.08, without revision-from-feedback 2.58, without CBR 3.41 (lower is better). Memento also finds planning adds more than CBR. GAP SEARCH UPDATE: re-read of DS-Agent confirms 2.08 / 2.58 / 3.41 but the removed piece is a bundle (feedback-driven re-ranking and adjustment), so it is not a clean copy-vs-revise test. Still one setting.
agent_test: Ablate: retrieve-and-copy vs retrieve-and-revise-from-failing-output at equal tokens.

claim: Memory can lower constraint satisfaction. Memp TravelPlanner hard-constraint for GPT-4o fell from 12.88 (no memory) to 5.50 to 9.76 under every memory policy, while commonsense score rose 71.93 to 79.94.
agent_test: Check that library reuse does not reduce checks passed; verify by code (G5).

claim: Reported CBR agent headline numbers mostly come from the authors' own benchmarks with small tests and single runs: CBR-RAG +1.94% cosine on 32 questions; GAIA 87.88 is Pass@3 on validation and test 79.40 uses a bank built on validation; AIME sets have 30 questions (1 question = 3.3 points); ReasoningBank single run per cell with no confidence interval. Treat as direction, not size.
agent_test: Use at least 5 seeds and paired tests on our own held-out sets.

claim: Which feature to index on depends on the task and on which description of the old case explains its outcome; neither pure surface nor pure abstract features are always right. Showing failed cases with explanations stops users discounting them. A design argument, not an experiment; Smyth and Keane's adaptation-guided retrieval was not opened.
agent_test: Key each stored subgoal by its goal plus its failure signature; test against goal-only keys.

claim: Early fielded CBR reported operational benefit: Compaq SMART/QuickSource about 20 percent fewer calls, 10 to 20 million dollars a year (extrapolated; about 500 cases, one-week sample, error margin about 5 percent). No controlled test; no replication found.
agent_test: Not testable on our agent; context only.

claim: Transformers fine-tuned on addition behave case-based: accuracy collapses on a held-out block (Leave-Square-Out) while random-split stays near 100%; Rule-Following Fine-Tuning fixes it (1 to 5 digit training, 12 digit above 95%). The paper uses 'case-based' for interpolation in weights, not an external case store.
agent_test: Probe our library tasks with a held-out structure split, not a random split, so memory is not credited for interpolation.

claim: Weights vs memory: CASCADE beat REINFORCE+LoRA on 9 of 12 tasks with k=1 and 12 of 12 with k=4, needing under 4 GB GPU memory; it failed when the base model never succeeded (MIMIC-IV, Qwen3-4B).
agent_test: No training in our agent; the failure condition (base never succeeds) implies the library needs some base successes.

claim: Verified subgoal libraries beat a no-library arm in the two systems that test reuse below the task level, but neither matches tokens or compute. LEGO-Prover (miniF2F-valid, 50 attempts): 50.4% with a growing lemma library vs 47.1% without; only 24% of 135 solved problems used a retrieved skill. ReGAL: verified helper functions beat retrieval of whole primitive programs from the same data (CodeLlama-13B LOGO 45.6 to 57.1; GPT-3.5 MATH +11.8), with ablations showing retry (LOGO 55.0 to 48.3) and curriculum (55.0 to 36.3) matter more than pruning or editing.
agent_test: Library of verified subgoal solutions vs no library vs whole-task library, at equal total tokens, on math, ARC-like and code items. Admit only items that pass a code or answer check.

claim: Keys that describe what a case does beat keys that describe how it looks, and keys ranked by measured usefulness beat nearest-neighbour similarity. Skill-KNN: Spider 78.3 vs 74.6 for the best raw-text key (oracle 78.6). EPR: GPT-Neo BREAK 31.9 vs BM25 26.0 and a case-based-reasoning baseline 25.7; one-shot 23.0 vs 15.2. Humans retrieve by structure when the cue carries a familiar relation label (Raynal et al. 2026, 0.46 vs 0.04 per participant). All tested on semantic parsing or recall, not on subgoals; the skill-description vocabulary was seeded by human-annotated demos.
agent_test: Three keys for the same subgoal library: raw subgoal text, LLM-written 'what it does' description, observed-success-weighted rank. Equal K and tokens.

claim: Similar-looking but unhelpful context hurts more than random context. GSM-IC: one irrelevant sentence leaves fewer than 30% of base problems solved consistently, worst with role-name overlap. RAG: high-score no-answer passages cut accuracy up to 67% while random passages added to the retrieved set raised Llama2 accuracy up to 35% (0.07 absolute). Dynamic Cheatsheet authors report retrieval 'can introduce confusion' when suboptimal examples are recalled.
agent_test: Seed the library with near-miss subgoals (same wording, different structure) and measure accuracy loss; compare with a relevance check before use.

claim: A retrieval gate can beat always-retrieve, but the only tested gate uses an outside popularity signal and works only for large models. Mallen et al. PopQA: retrieval turned correct to wrong for 10% of questions and wrong to correct for 17%; adaptive retrieval with GPT-3 reached 46.5%, 5.3 points above any non-adaptive method; small models (under 10B) gain little because they almost always need retrieval. Evo-Memory shows memory below no-memory on BabyAI (success 0.52 to 0.56 vs 0.61), which is the same pattern in agents. No study gates case lookup on similarity to the nearest stored case.
agent_test: Compare always-retrieve vs skip-if-nearest-similarity-below-t vs skip-if-self-solve-succeeds, binned by similarity of the new item to the library.

claim: Filtering stored examples for verified correctness changes the shape of the K curve. Many-shot ICL on MATH500 (Gemini 1.5 Pro): human-written solutions peak near 125 examples then decline; model-generated solutions kept only when the final answer is correct plateau near 25 examples at about +5 points and do not decline at very large K.
agent_test: At equal total tokens, sweep K with verified-only vs unfiltered library entries.

claim: In a 2026 conceptual re-run of the Fortress-to-Radiation paradigm (Spanish undergraduates, N=128, one story and a summary task) only 5% solved the Radiation problem without a hint and 36% after a hint, well below the 41% and 85% quoted from Gick and Holyoak. Generating an analogous situation first raised spontaneous success to 63% (N=40) from 43% without spatial cues. The design differs from the original (one story, different scoring), so this is not a failed replication, but the 85% figure is not reproduced.
agent_test: Before library lookup, have the agent restate the current subgoal in library vocabulary (generate an analog), and compare lookup hit rate with raw-text cueing.

claim: Large reported memory gains sit on templated or single-algorithm tasks. Game of 24: GPT-4o 10 to 99 (Dynamic Cheatsheet, model stored a Python solver), GPT-4 3.0 to 82.4 (Buffer of Thoughts) while a plain program prompt (PAL) already reached 64.0. Evo-Memory gain correlates with within-dataset similarity (r=0.717 and 0.563). No study re-tests these gains on structurally new problems or with contamination removed.
agent_test: Evaluate any library on a held-out structure split and on problems written after the model's cutoff; report gain separately for templated and new-structure items.
